transcription_flags.issue: Handbook: 'Where percentages are quoted, the total may not add up to 100% because of error in the rounding up process.' Outcome and where-found percentages are stored as printed and are not renormalised.
Glossary defines Youth as 13 - 16 yr; the category pages (10, 11) are titled Youth (13 - 15 years).
Alzheimer's text says '50% are found within 0.6 miles of IPP'; the table on the same page gives 50% = 0.80 km / 0.50 miles. Both stored as printed.
Despondents (Koester) 100% printed as '32.0' km (one decimal); stored as 32.0.
Hikers (Hill) 100% printed as '15.0' miles (one decimal); stored as 15.0.
Sample size differs between UK outcome, distance and where-found tables for some categories (e.g. Misc Adults: outcomes n=30, distance n=25). Each table keeps its own printed n.
The 100% row is the single furthest case found (e.g. 132 km for UK youths and despondents), not a statistical bound; it dominates the outer ring and the grid's outer band.
The handbook gives distances in 10% stages instead of the traditional 25%/median/75% zones. There are no 25%, 75% or 95% rows; any such ring is linearly interpolated by the tool and marked so.
Hunters: the UK study has no equivalent category; only the Hill (1997) table exists.
Fishermen, climbers and skiers have notes only (Syrotuck / Mitchell); no distance table. Organised groups have only the UK table. No category in the handbook is split by terrain.
